questions.stem: Which of the following is a perfect square?
questions.keySolution:
Check which number is a perfect square:
\(169 = 13 \times 13 = 13^2\)
Therefore, \(169\) is a perfect square (root = 13)

questions.stem: What is \(\sqrt{196}\)?
questions.keySolution:
Finding the square root:
\(196 = 14 \times 14\)
Therefore, \(\sqrt{196} = 14\)

questions.stem: Is \(225\) a perfect square?
options: No, it cannot be perfect square
Yes, but its root is irrational
questions.keySolution:
Check if 225 is perfect square:
\(15 \times 15 = 225\)
So \(225 = 15^2\)
Therefore, 225 is a perfect square with root 15

questions.stem: Using prime factorization, check if \(144\) is a perfect square:
questions.keySolution:
Prime factorization of 144:
\(144 = 2^4 \times 3^2\)
All exponents are even, so 144 is a perfect square
\(\sqrt{144} = 12\)

questions.stem: Is \(180\) a perfect square? (Using prime factorization)
questions.keySolution:
Prime factorization of 180:
\(180 = 2^2 \times 3^2 \times 5\)
Exponents: 2(even), 2(even), 1(odd)
Since 5 has odd exponent, 180 is NOT a perfect square

\((15)^2 = 15 \times 15 = 225\)

Which number must be multiplied by \(75\) to make it a perfect square?
questions.keySolution:
Prime factorization of 75: \(75 = 3 \times 5^2\)
For perfect square, all exponents must be even. 3 has exponent 1 (odd)
Multiply by 3: \(75 \times 3 = 225 = 3^2 \times 5^2 = (15)^2\)

questions.stem: What number must be divided by \(98\) to make it a perfect square?
questions.keySolution:
Prime factorization of 98: \(98 = 2 \times 7^2\)
For perfect square, all exponents must be even. 2 has exponent 1 (odd)
Divide by 2: \(98 ÷ 2 = 49 = 7^2\)

questions.stem: Using identity \((a^2 - b^2) = (a + b)(a - b)\), simplify \((25 - 9)\):
questions.keySolution:
Using identity: \((5)^2 - (3)^2 = (5+3)(5-3) = 8 \times 2 = 16\)
Direct: \(25 - 9 = 16\)
Both methods give same answer

questions.stem: What is the perfect square between \(40\) and \(50\)?
questions.keySolution:
Check squares: \(6^2 = 36\) (too small), \(7^2 = 49\) (in range), \(8^2 = 64\) (too large)
Therefore, 49 is the perfect square between 40 and 50

questions.stem: The unit digit of \(37^2\) is:
questions.keySolution:
Unit digit of 37 is 7. Square of 7: \(7^2 = 49\) (unit digit = 9)
Therefore, unit digit of \(37^2\) is 9

questions.stem: Which number ending in these digits CANNOT be a perfect square?
questions.keySolution:
Perfect squares can only end in: 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 9
They CANNOT end in: 2, 3, 7, 8
Therefore, a number ending in 3 cannot be a perfect square

questions.stem: Find greatest perfect square that divides \(180\):
questions.keySolution:
Prime factorization of 180: \(180 = 2^2 \times 3^2 \times 5\)
For greatest perfect square factor, take even powers: \(2^2 \times 3^2 = 36\)
Verify: \(180 ÷ 36 = 5\)
